# alchemeR

<!-- badges: start -->

[![R](https://github.com/grousell/alchemeR/actions/workflows/r.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/grousell/alchemeR/actions/workflows/r.yml)
<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of alchemeR is to provide tools to access Alchemer survey data from their API and pull into an R environment. More information on the Alchemer API and set up can be found here: <https://apihelp.alchemer.com/help>

## Installation

You can install the development version of alchemeR from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("grousell/alchemeR")
```

## Credentials

Create an API token and secret key in Alchemer and put them in your `.Renviron`
(`usethis::edit_r_environ()`), then restart R:

```
ALCHEMER_API_TOKEN=your-token
ALCHEMER_API_SECRET=your-secret
```

All functions read these two variables by default. To use `keyring` instead,
pass `token = keyring::key_get("alchemer", "token")` and
`secret_key = keyring::key_get("alchemer", "secret")`. The package only sends
read-only (GET) requests and never prints your credentials.

## Example

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(alchemeR)

all_surveys()                                   # one row per survey

df   <- fetch_survey(123, dir = "data_raw")       # a labelled tibble; keeps data_raw/survey_123.rds (folder is created)
dict <- fetch_data_dictionary(123)              # one row per answer option
```

`fetch_survey()` prints one line saying what it did, for example
`Survey 123: incremental pull (37 rows changed), 4 requests, 2.1 s`.
The request count is the number of API calls; a call retried after a rate limit or server error counts once. Use `suppressMessages()` to silence the line.

### What happens when you run it again

* Within `min_age` seconds (default 600) of the last check: the file is read, no request is made.
* Otherwise it asks Alchemer whether anything changed (2 requests). If not, the file is kept; if so, only recently updated responses are downloaded and merged.
* Everything is downloaded again when the survey was edited, an older response was deleted, `include_test` changed, or the oldest rows are over `full_refresh_days` (default 90) days old and the survey is active. The message tells you why and roughly how many requests it needs.
* `refresh = "full"` forces a full download; `refresh = "local"` reads the file without any request.
* A failed download never damages the file. If the file cannot be written (open in another program, locked by a synced folder), you get a warning and the data anyway.

### The data

* Columns: `survey_id`, `id`, `status`, `is_test_data`, dates (Toronto time), `response_time`, `language`, `link_id`, `data_quality` (JSON text), then one column per answer in questionnaire order: `Q<id>`, or `Q<id>_<option id>` for each option of checkbox and rank items (table rows use their own ids), and `fetched_at`. Single sign-on surveys also get `url_<name>` columns (a URL-shaped name such as `http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/givenname` becomes `url_givenname`, or its full cleaned name if two would clash); other URL variables are not kept.
* Question text is the `label` attribute of each column (shown by RStudio's viewer, `gtsummary`, `sjPlot`). `bind_rows()` drops labels.
* Numeric text boxes, sliders and rank items are numbers; everything else is text. A value in a numeric item that is not a number (for example `12 kg`) becomes `NA`, with a warning that shows its shape but not its value.
* A choice answer holds the option's *reporting value*, not its title. Recode with the dictionary:
  `dict |> dplyr::filter(question_id == "Q3") |> dplyr::select(option_value, option_label)`.
* The dictionary is also in `attr(df, "alchemer")$dictionary`, next to the survey metadata.
* All statuses are returned (`Complete`, `Partial`, `Disqualified`); filter on `status`. Test data is excluded unless `include_test = TRUE`; use a separate `dir` if you need both.
* Signature images are not kept (only the typed name), and identifiers such as IP address, session and contact ids are not kept. Hidden values and open-text answers are returned as collected.
* Responses deleted in Alchemer disappear from the file at the next full download (or when they fall in the recent window).

### Recipes

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Complete responses since a date, one per respondent (most answers, then latest)
library(dplyr)
answers <- c("Q20", "Q21", "Q22")                 # the questions that matter
df |>
  filter(
    status == "Complete",
    date_submitted >= as.POSIXct("2026-10-06", tz = "America/Toronto")
  ) |>
  mutate(n_answered = rowSums(!is.na(pick(all_of(answers))))) |>
  filter(n_answered > 0) |>
  arrange(desc(n_answered), desc(id)) |>
  distinct(url_NameID, .keep_all = TRUE)           # single sign-on id; text, join it as text

# Question text (the column label) instead of retyping it
purrr::map_chr(df[answers], \(x) attr(x, "label"))
```

* **Dates are date-times in Toronto time.** Compare them with a date-time as above. Do not use `as.Date()` on them: it takes the UTC day, so an evening response (after 8 p.m. in summer) lands on the next day.
* **Ids from single sign-on are text.** Keep leading zeros by joining text to text (`student_no` in your student table is text too).
* **A warning about answers "not placed in a column"** means the survey contains an answer shape the package does not know; some answers are missing from the table. Please report it.

### Several surveys, other tools

```{r, eval=FALSE}
ids <- c(123, 456)
all_data <- purrr::map(ids, fetch_survey, refresh = "local") |> dplyr::bind_rows()
arrow::write_parquet(fetch_survey(123), "survey_123.parquet")   # for Python, Power BI
```

### Archive a whole account

Copy the report and render it with Quarto:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
file.copy(system.file("quarto", "Archive_account.qmd", package = "alchemeR"), ".")
# quarto render Archive_account.qmd -P archive_dir:my_archive
```

The report lists each survey's status, warnings and errors, and every run appends to `archive_log.csv` in the archive folder.
